deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a topological space with a finite partition (X_i)_{i∈I} into 'leaves'. F_p is the family of unions of leaves. The axioms are:
1) each closure cl(X_i) is a union of leaves (frontier condition);
2) cl(X_i) = cl(X_j) implies i = j.
Such a partition is an 'admissible stratification'. It is 'strict' if moreover
3) each X_i is connected.

Claim (started on the previous page, finished here). Given 1) and 2), condition 3) is equivalent to axiom f) of §1 for F_p: every A in F_p (first 'locally closed', which is then struck out) has finitely many connected components, all lying in F_p.

f) ⇒ 3). X_i is locally closed and belongs to F_p, so its components lie in F_p. A nonempty X_i is a minimal nonempty element of F_p, so X_i is connected. (Local closedness follows from 1) and 2). If X_i meets cl(X_j) with j ≠ i, then by 1) X_i ⊂ cl(X_j). Hence cl(X_i) = cl(X_j) whenever X_j ⊂ cl(X_i), which contradicts 2). So X_i is cl(X_i) minus a finite union of closed sets.)

3) ⇒ f). Take any A in F_p. Replace X by A with the induced partition; this still satisfies 1), 2), 3).
- For 1): the closure of X_i in A is cl(X_i) ∩ A, which is again a union of leaves.
- For 2), the only non-trivial check: suppose cl(X_i) ∩ A = cl(X_j) ∩ A. Then X_i ⊂ cl(X_j) and X_j ⊂ cl(X_i). So cl(X_i) = cl(X_j), hence i = j.

This reduces the claim to showing that the components of X are unions of leaves. The leaves are connected and cover X, so each component is a union of leaves (indeed of closures of leaves). There are therefore finitely many components, and being closed and finite in number, they are open.

The page then begins the reformulation. Let Y = X/R ≅ I be the quotient, a finite topological space. The next page shows:
- the closure of {i} corresponds to cl(X_i);
- incidence of leaves is the specialization order;
- 2) says Y is 'pré-sobre', i.e. T0;
- 1) says X → Y is an open map.
So finite cellular decompositions correspond to finite T0 quotients X → Y with open quotient map. This serves the axiomatics of 'tame' families F of subsets (an o-minimal-like setting) in the Topologie modérée notes, leading to F-admissible decompositions in §3.
errors: No real errors. The 'minimality' step in f) ⇒ 3) tacitly uses that X_i is a minimal NONEMPTY element of F_p. It also uses that X_i is locally closed, which follows from 1) and 2) as reconstructed but is not argued on this page.

The struck-out 'loc. fermé' shows Grothendieck noticed the argument works for every A in F_p, not only locally closed ones. This is correct, since the induced partition on any union of leaves still satisfies 1)–3).
Minor: the components are said to be unions of closures cl(X_i). It suffices, and is cleaner, to say unions of leaves X_i. The finiteness and openness of the components then follow as stated.

ideas.what: Finite stratification with the frontier condition: closures are unions of strata and distinct strata have distinct closures (cellular decomposition).
ideas.modern_name: Stratification satisfying the frontier condition / finite cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratifications); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5–6 discusses tame topology and stratifications informally, not this lemma.

ideas.what: Strata are connected iff every union of strata has finitely many components, each a union of strata.
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness of cells / finiteness of components in o-minimal-type structures

ideas.what: Stratification identified with a finite quotient space X → I. Incidence equals the specialization order, the frontier condition equals openness of the quotient map, and distinct closures equal the T0 property ('pré-sobre'). Begun here, completed on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Stratified space as a map to a finite poset with the Alexandrov topology (exit-path / exodromy framework)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); Treumann; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; Barwick–Glasman–Haine (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Not in the published texts in this form, as far as I know.

missed.claim: In 1974 Grothendieck was already encoding finite stratifications as finite T0 quotient spaces with open quotient map, identifying incidence with specialization. Modern stratified homotopy theory adopted the map-to-a-finite-poset viewpoint only around 2009–2017. Grothendieck's variant, requiring an open quotient map, is slightly different from Lurie's merely continuous map.
missed.quote: Soit Y = X/R (≃ I) l'espace quotient. C'est un espace top fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the poset-stratification formalism. The 'open map' condition, which is equivalent to the frontier condition, is a natural refinement sometimes discussed separately in the exodromy literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The connectedness lemma itself is routine. The page's interest is in starting the identification of stratifications with finite T0 quotients and open quotient maps, an early anticipation of the modern poset-stratified viewpoint. The full statement is on the next page, and it is a natural observation.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'A ∈ F_p' looks more like 'pas néc.' / 'pas nécess.' (i.e. 'not necessarily locally closed', with 'loc.' struck) than 'pas vide'. This matches the mathematics, where local closedness is not needed.

Last line: after 'Si i ∈ I', the closure of {i} is probably meant ('{i}‾ le plus petit [fermé]'), continuing onto the next page's 'fermé ... correspondant au plus petit ensemble fermé de X contenant X_i'.
'or X_i étant un {+élément+} ≠ ∅ minimal de F_p' is correct in sense. The word above may be an abbreviation such as 'élt'.
